thread:
maria: Heads-up: tight maintenance window tonight 23:45-00:15 UTC. Need finalization on pin, staged shift plan, and explicit rollback owners for API/runtime/router/console. Release notes: https://confluence.redwood/release/three-service-2026
kevin: OK. versions?
lisa: API=2.4.2, runtime=3.7.1-rc1, router=1.9.0, console=0.10.0. Runtime includes a new batched-kernel path so it's higher risk.
chao: Proposal: canary 3% -> 20% -> 70% -> 100% with 6m observation windows. Hold at each step until manual ack unless hard failure.
maria: Agree. No auto-promote beyond 20% without ops ack. We'll pin the runtime model to quant-8 for the first 30 minutes to minimize mem pressure.
kevin: Rollback triggers (suggested):
- runtime: any sustained GPU memory alloc failures (OOM or nvmlError) OR >1.5% 5xx over a 5m rolling window -> immediate rollback.
- api: error rate >=0.8% for 10m OR p95 latency increase >200ms -> rollback.
- router: route mismatch rate >0.2% OR header-drop anomalies -> rollback.
- console: frontend JS errors >1% or failing healthchecks -> rollback.
lisa: Owners: ops-oncall executes rollback commands. Engineering leads must ACK within 5m for a rollback to proceed. If lead not reachable, ops will follow pre-agreed thresholds.
chao: We'll enable a temporary header-swap flag so QA can route 100% of a subset client to the new router for deeper validation during the 20% and 70% stages.
kevin: Add smoke evals after 70% and again 1h post-cutover. If any eval metric regresses >2.5% on primary quality metric, we revert.
maria: Deploy-bot dry-run looked good. When we start, we'll post a single-line summary to #release-war-room and keep telemetry aggressive for 90m after.
deploy-bot: Deploy scheduler engaged. Canary plan queued. Command used:
```
/deploy start --svc api=2.4.2 runtime=3.7.1-rc1 router=1.9.0 console=0.10.0 --canary 3,20,70 --hold-on 20 --window 30m --dry-run=false
```
deploy-bot: Tip: canary-tag=canary-561235 for logs and metrics queries.
ops-oncall: I'm on for the window 23:40-00:20 UTC. I'll run the rollback command if we hit infra thresholds. Tag me @ops-oncall if you want me to hold at any stage.
lisa: I'll watch runtime logs for `nvmlError`, `cudaMalloc` and `batch_kernel_mismatch`. Chao will own router-level checks.
chao: I'll toggle header-swap for the client subset when at 20% and report.
kevin: Agreement: if 20% stage sees non-actionable but concerning spikes, we hold and run extended 15m warmup rather than immediate rollback. Any hard infra (OOM, node crashes) -> rollback.
maria: Final: start at 23:45 UTC. I'll ping #release-war-room with the short summary and link to notes. :rocket:
